source: NCERT Class XI, Themes in World History, Ch. 2 (An Empire Across Three Continents).

sections.heading: 1. The Roman Empire — Extent
points: The **Roman Empire** spanned **three continents** — Europe, Asia (West Asia) and Africa (North Africa) — around the **Mediterranean Sea** ('our sea').
Two powers dominated: the **Roman** and the **Iranian (Parthian/Sasanian)** empires.
Time frame studied: roughly **1st century BCE to 6th–7th centuries CE**.

sections.heading: 2. Political and Social Structure
points: Key institutions: the **emperor**, the **Senate (aristocracy)**, and the **army** (a paid, professional force — a decisive political factor).
**Augustus** established the Principate (27 BCE) after the Republic; emperors ruled with the Senate's cooperation in theory.
Society had **great social/economic diversity**: senators, equites (knights), the middle classes, plebeians, slaves.
**Slavery** was widespread but debated; **the family** and the position of women (with property rights, though patriarchal) were notable.

sections.heading: 3. Economy and Everyday Life
points: A well-developed **economy**: coinage (silver denarius), trade across the Mediterranean, wine/olive oil (amphorae), grain from Egypt/North Africa.
**Cities** were centres of civic life with amenities; the empire depended on a network of **towns, ports and roads**.
Wide use of **money, banking and wage labour**; **third-century crisis** brought strain.

sections.heading: 4. Late Antiquity and Religion
points: **Late Antiquity** (4th–7th c.) = period of great cultural and religious change.
**Christianity** spread and became the state religion under **Constantine** (4th c.); the empire was later divided (Western and Eastern/Byzantine).
The rise of **Islam (7th c.)** transformed the region; the Western Roman Empire declined.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Roman Empire spanned three continents around the Mediterranean ('our sea').
Two great powers: Roman and Iranian (Parthian/Sasanian).
Augustus began the Principate (27 BCE); army was a key political factor.
Constantine adopted Christianity (4th c.); it became the state religion.
Late Antiquity = era of religious/cultural change; rise of Islam (7th c.).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The empire crossed **three continents** (Europe, Asia, Africa) around the **Mediterranean**.
The **army** was a **paid, professional** force and a major political power.
**Constantine** was the emperor linked with the rise of **Christianity**.
The rival of Rome in the east was the **Iranian (Parthian/Sasanian)** empire.
